reasoning:
Torah #122 is a 4-line aphoristic teaching with a strict binary structure. The gap analysis (torah_122_additions.json) identified exactly two proposed bechina pairs from the source text:

(1) נֵצַח יִשְׂרָאֵל ↔ אֱמֶת [good, Package 1 — divine nitzachon = truth]
(2) מִדַּת הַנִּצָּחוֹן ↔ דְּחִיַּת הָאֱמֶת [evil, Package 2 — human nitzachon = rejection of truth]

These two pairs are already fully captured in the two packages of torah_122_packages.json. No additional conceptual domain was found in the source text that would constitute a new, independent thematic cluster.

The teaching has no third pole, no sub-cluster, and no additional concepts that introduce a new domain. The four nodes across the two packages exhaust all conceptual content of the Torah.

The two packages themselves are new in the sense that the dataset has zero edges for Torah #122 and these packages represent the full proposed dataset enrichment — but they are not 'new packages beyond what the packages file already proposes.' The new_packages.json file by design identifies proposed packages that were NOT captured in the packages.json file (i.e., packages that emerge from gap analysis and would constitute a third or further cluster). No such cluster exists here.

structural_note.description: Torah #122 is a micro-teaching of maximal compression. It operates entirely on the polysemy of a single Hebrew word (נֵצַח/נִצָּחוֹן = contentiousness/victory AND the Eternal One of Israel), using that double-meaning to contrast two modes of existence: human contentiousness (which structurally rejects truth) vs. God's eternal nature (which IS truth). The entire teaching is a single proposition with a positive and negative pole — identical in structure to the universe's good/evil mirror but expressed through linguistic rather than explicit conceptual bechinot.
structural_note.good_evil_mirror: The good/evil mirror in Torah #122 is the tightest in the corpus: a single word bifurcates into its holy meaning (נֵצַח יִשְׂרָאֵל = the Eternal of Israel = truth) and its human-fallen meaning (מִדַּת הַנִּצָּחוֹן = human contentiousness = rejection of truth). Package 1 (good) and Package 2 (evil) are the mirror pair. No further mirror structure exists because the teaching has only two poles.
structural_note.dataset_enrichment_note: The primary dataset enrichment task for Torah #122 is the population of the two proposed bechina edges in torah_122_additions.json (edges proposed_122_01 and proposed_122_02). Once these are added to torahData.js with reference 122, the bechina graph for this Torah will be complete. No eitza edges are proposed because the teaching has no causal chain structure.
structural_note.note_on_bechina_vs_eitza_boundary: The second proposed edge (מִדַּת הַנִּצָּחוֹן ↔ דְּחִיַּת הָאֱמֶת) sits on the boundary between bechina and eitza classification. The source text describes the relationship as behavioral/structural incompatibility ('does not tolerate truth') which could be read as causal (nitzachon → rejection). However, the Rebbe's framing as an axiomatic, definitional truth ('זֶה מְבֹרָר מְאֹד' — this is very well established) supports classification as a bechina (shared essential nature: human contentiousness IS truth-rejection as its essential quality). The dataset team should review this edge upon entry. If classified as eitza, it would move to the eitza layer but would not affect the package structure since the teaching's bechina architecture is fully captured by the first edge alone (נֵצַח יִשְׂרָאֵל ↔ אֱמֶת).
